source: Karnataka NMMS GMAT 2019 question paper, NMMS - GMAT (K-8) P-1 (pyq/NMMS GMAT P-1 K-E QP_1.pdf). The paper has no answer key, so every answer here is worked out by us.

sections.directions: Complete the following number series by choosing the correct number from the given choices.
The order of the letters that need to come in the boxes to complete a certain pattern is:
Identify the wrong number in the given series.
Four groups of numbers / pairs of numbers / groups of letters are given for each question, of which three are alike and one is different. Select the different one.
The following Venn diagrams show the relationship among the three given objects. Identify the appropriate diagram to show the relationship.
Complete the given analogy by selecting the correct answer from the alternatives.
Complete the given analogy by selecting the correct answers from the alternatives.
In the questions given below the numbers in the figures are related. Identify their relationship and find the missing number.
Find the missing number/letter in the given matrices.
Choose and substitute the correct set of signs in place of * sequentially, selecting from the given alternatives, to make the equations meaningful.
Find out which numbers/signs should be interchanged to get the correct equation.
The following questions are based on the given intersecting figures. Each figure represents a group.
Identify the number of specified geometric shapes in the given diagram and mark the correct answer.
In the following questions, a word is written according to some code. Identify the code of the other word given below.
The following questions are based on the figures in series. Pick from the options what will come next.

In the following questions, a sheet of paper is folded, punched and part of it is cut (shaded region), and all these are shown by figures. If the paper is unfolded, how does it appear? Select the answer from the alternatives.
In each question there is a figure to the left of a mirror, shown by lines, and its possible images are given on the right. Choose the correct mirror image of the figure.
In the following figures, a part of the figure is missing. Identify the missing part among the four alternatives given.
A sheet of paper as shown in the figure is folded to form a cube. Answer the following questions.

In each of the given figures, there is a relationship between the first two figures. The same relation is between the next two figures, but one is missing. Find the missing figure from the given alternatives.
In the given questions, there are figures or numbers above the line. Their water images are given below. Find the correct water image of the figures from the given alternatives.

questions.prompt: In the given series, how many times does a prime number appear between two odd numbers?
questions.rule: Go through the series one place at a time and mark every place that fits, then count the marks.
questions.working: They are: 3 7 5, 7 5 9, 1 3 7, 5 3 9. That makes 4.

questions.prompt: In the given series, how many times does '3' come right after an odd number?
questions.rule: Go through the series one place at a time and mark every place that fits, then count the marks.
questions.working: They are: 1 3, 3 3, 3 3, 5 3, 7 3, 9 3. That makes 6.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Wild animals, lions, tigers?
questions.rule: Lions and tigers are both wild animals, so both circles sit inside the wild animals circle.
questions.note: Lions and tigers should be two separate circles inside "wild animals", which is not among the options. Diagram c (two overlapping circles inside a big one) is the closest; check the official key.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Women, mothers, nurses?
questions.rule: All mothers are women, so that circle is inside. Some nurses are women and some are mothers, but some nurses are men, so the nurses circle cuts both and goes outside.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Husband, wife, child?
questions.rule: No one is two of these at once, so the three circles are separate.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Professors, doctors, engineers?
questions.rule: A professor can also be a doctor or an engineer, so the circles overlap.
questions.note: All three groups can share people, so all three circles should overlap one another. In diagram b the two outer circles do not touch; it is the closest option. Check the official key.

questions.prompt: Sonu is the son of Sarika. Reeta is the daughter of Sarika. If Sarika is the sister of Raju, how is Reeta related to Raju?
questions.rule: Reeta is Sarika's daughter, and Sarika is Raju's sister.
questions.working: A sister's daughter is a niece.

questions.prompt: A girl introduced a boy as the son of the daughter of the father of her uncle. How is the boy related to the girl?
questions.rule: The father of her uncle is her grandfather. His daughter is the girl's mother (or aunt).
questions.working: The son of her mother is her brother; Brother is the only option that fits.

questions.rule: Add the numbers inside both the rectangle and the triangle.

questions.prompt: Find the number of squares in the given figure.
questions.rule: In a 4 × 4 grid, count the squares of each size.
questions.working: 16 small + 9 of 2 × 2 + 4 of 3 × 3 + 1 big = 30

questions.prompt: Find the number of semicircles in the given figure.
questions.rule: A circle cut by one straight line through its centre makes 2 semicircles; cut by two lines across each other it makes 4.
questions.working: The 3 circles round the centre are cut by both lines: 3 × 4 = 12. The 6 small circles are cut by one line each: 6 × 2 = 12. 12 + 12 = 24

questions.prompt: Find the number of triangles in the given figure.
questions.rule: Five lines come down from the top. Any two of them make a triangle with the base, and with the short line across.
questions.working: With the base: any 2 of the 5 lines, 10 triangles. With the line across, which meets 3 of the lines: 3 more. 10 + 3 = 13

questions.prompt: Find the number of parallelograms in the given figure.
questions.rule: The lines run in three directions. A parallelogram needs two lines from one direction and two from another.
questions.working: Slanting both ways: 3 × 3 = 9. Flat lines with each slant: 3 + 3 = 6. 9 + 6 = 15

questions.prompt: The present ages of Shashank and Prashanth are in the ratio 4 : 3. If Shashank will be 26 years old after 6 years, what is the present age of Prashanth?
questions.rule: Find Shashank's age now, then use the ratio.
questions.working: Shashank is 26 − 6 = 20 now. 20 is 4 parts, so 1 part is 5 and Prashanth is 3 × 5 = 15

questions.prompt: The sum of three different numbers is equal to their product. Which is the biggest number among them?
questions.rule: Try small numbers: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 and 1 × 2 × 3 = 6.
questions.working: The numbers are 1, 2 and 3, so the biggest is 3

questions.prompt: A man started walking from his house towards the south. After walking 6 km he turned to his left and walked 5 km, then he walked a further 3 km after turning left. Again he turned left and walked 9 km. How far is he from his house now?
questions.rule: Draw the walk. Facing south, a left turn faces east; then north; then west. The straight-line distance home is found with Pythagoras.
questions.working: He ends 6 − 3 = 3 km south and 9 − 5 = 4 km west of home: √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 km

questions.prompt: This year "Teachers' Day" is celebrated on a Thursday. On what day will "Teachers' Day" be celebrated next year?
questions.rule: Teachers' Day is 5 September. A year later the day moves on by 1, or by 2 if 29 February comes in between.
questions.working: This paper is from 2019 (5 September 2019 was a Thursday). From then to 5 September 2020, 29 February 2020 comes in between: 2 days after Thursday is Saturday

questions.prompt: This year "Independence Day" is celebrated on a Thursday. On what day will "Republic Day" be celebrated next year?
questions.rule: Independence Day is 15 August and Republic Day is 26 January. Count the days in between and divide by 7.
questions.working: From 15 August to 26 January: 16 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 26 = 164 days. 164 = 23 × 7 + 3, so 3 days after Thursday: Sunday

questions.prompt: PALM is coded as UEOO in a certain language. How is YEAR coded?
questions.rule: The letters move +5, +4, +3, +2: P → U, A → E, L → O, M → O.
questions.working: Y + 5 = D (after Z, start again at A), E + 4 = I, A + 3 = D, R + 2 = T: DIDT

questions.prompt: If EARTH is coded as 41590 and PACE as 2134, how is PEACH coded?
questions.rule: Each letter has its own digit: E = 4, A = 1, R = 5, T = 9, H = 0, P = 2, C = 3.
questions.working: P E A C H = 2 4 1 3 0

questions.prompt: If FORGIVE is coded as DPPHGWC in a certain language, how is REQUEST coded?
questions.rule: The letters move −2 and +1 in turn: F → D, O → P, R → P, G → H, I → G, V → W, E → C.
questions.working: R − 2 = P, E + 1 = F, Q − 2 = O, U + 1 = V, E − 2 = C, S + 1 = T, T − 2 = R: PFOVCTR

questions.prompt: If KODAGU is coded as NRGDJX in a certain language, how is TIPTUR coded?
questions.rule: Every letter moves 3 places forward: K → N, O → R, D → G.
questions.working: T → W, I → L, P → S, T → W, U → X, R → U: WLSWXU

questions.prompt: If TAG is coded as 112, how is PEN coded?
questions.rule: Add the letter places and multiply by 4: T + A + G = 20 + 1 + 7 = 28, and 28 × 4 = 112.

questions.working: Unfolding the 2nd fold copies each hole across the line from the centre to the bottom right corner; unfolding the 1st copies them across the diagonal. That gives a pair near the bottom left and top right corners, and a pair on each side of the centre: C.

questions.prompt: A sheet of paper as shown in the figure is folded to form a cube. Which face is opposite ○?
questions.rule: In a straight line of squares, the 1st and 3rd are opposite.
questions.working: The column reads △, ○, +, ⊠: △ is opposite +, and ○ is opposite ⊠.

questions.prompt: A sheet of paper as shown in the figure is folded to form a cube. Which two faces are opposite each other?
questions.rule: Fold it round face 3: 2 folds up behind, 4 to the right, 1 to the left (beside 2), 5 to the front (below 4), and 6 lands on top.
questions.working: So 3 is opposite 6, 2 is opposite 5, and 1 is opposite 4.

questions.prompt: A sheet of paper as shown in the figure is folded to form a cube. Which face is opposite B?
questions.rule: Fold it round face D: C folds up behind, E to the right, F to the front, B to the left (beside C), and A lands on top.
questions.working: So D is opposite A, C is opposite F, and B is opposite E.

questions.prompt: When the unfolded cube shown is folded, which cube shows the correct numbers on its faces?
questions.rule: First find the opposite pairs: 1–3 and 2–4 (in the column), and 5–6 (on opposite sides). Two opposite faces can never be seen together.
questions.working: B shows 6 and 5, C shows 1 and 3, D shows 4 and 2, so they are wrong. A (4, 1 and 6) also has the faces the right way round.

questions.prompt: A dice is thrown four times and its four positions are shown. What number is on the face opposite the face with '2' on it?
questions.rule: A face can't be opposite any face seen next to it.
questions.working: 5 is seen next to 6, 4, 3 and 1, so the face opposite 5 is 2.

questions.rule: The arrow turns a quarter turn clockwise. The two small shapes turn a quarter turn the other way, so the right one goes to the top and the left one to the bottom, where it is filled in.

questions.rule: The three shapes, one inside another, each move one place out, and the outer one moves to the middle: circle–square–triangle becomes triangle–circle–square.
questions.working: Triangle–circle–square becomes square–triangle–circle: a square with a triangle inside, and a circle inside that: D.

questions.rule: The inside and outside shapes swap, and the one dot becomes three dots in a column.
questions.working: The square goes outside and the pentagon inside, with three dots: C.

questions.rule: In the second pair, the top left shape gains two sides, the top right and bottom left swap their counts (1 and 2), and the shaded shape in the bottom right becomes plain.
questions.working: So the square becomes a hexagon, ↑ becomes ↑↑, ↑↑ becomes ↑, and the shaded circle becomes plain: C.
